title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Burson Person
tiers.description: All Directors and Senior Management (each director, CEO, CFO, COO, Company Secretary, KMP) and any other person designated a Burson Person by the Board in writing, plus any company or trust controlled by such a person.

tiers.name: Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: seeks consent from the chair of the Board (or the chair of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee in the chair of the Board's absence).

tiers.name: Other Directors, Company Secretary and Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Distinguished only for clearance: seeks consent from the chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee, or failing that the chair of the Board or the chair of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee.

tiers.name: Other Burson Persons
tiers.description: Any other Burson Person; distinguished only for clearance, which is sought from the Company Secretary (or the CEO in the Company Secretary's absence).

tiers.name: Associates

rules.detail: Options and other derivative instruments over Burson securities are 'securities' for Trading Window and consent purposes. Dealing is permitted only within a Trading Window (or under a 4.3 exceptional-circumstances approval) with prior consent under 4.2, and is banned outright if short-term or speculative.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy is issued in the name of Burson Group Limited, which was later renamed Bapcor Limited (ASX: BAP); the ABN and trading windows/mechanics are otherwise unaffected.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Confirms the document is the correct, applicable policy for BAP notwithstanding the different company name on its face.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Burson securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights under a loan or security agreement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Gives the bank confidence that if it enforces its security and sells the collared shares, that disposal is an exempted dealing under the policy (only after-the-fact notice to the Authorising Officer is required), not a breach or a dealing needing fresh consent.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar is not possible over unvested Burson/Bapcor shares or vested shares still subject to a holding lock: section 5.2 bans all 'protection arrangements' (hedging, short selling beyond holding, anything limiting economic risk or profiting from a price fall) and section 5.3 bans granting any security or margin lending over such shares, with no consent pathway. Once the shares are vested and free of any holding lock, the same collar and loan-security package is permitted, but only within a Trading Window (or under a 4.3 exceptional-circumstances approval), subject to prior consent from the relevant Authorising Officer under 4.2, a confirmation of no Inside Information, and a post-trade confirmation. The consent chain differs by seniority (Board chair, Audit & Risk Committee chair, or Company Secretary/CEO) but all Burson Persons follow the same substantive rules. If the bank later needs to enforce its security and sell the shares, that sale is an exempted dealing requiring only after-the-fact notice, not fresh clearance. No minimum shareholding requirement is referenced.
